post.description:
Request cancellation of an in-progress run.

The response carries the actual durable status. When
`cancellation_requested` is true, Temporal accepted the stop request;
continue polling until a terminal status is returned. Results and charges

get.description:
Server-Sent Events: the agents' and subagents' turn summaries as they are written, in order.

New durable summaries are checked every two seconds while the stream is open.

Frames:
- `sessions` — every agent session, sent first and again whenever one starts, finishes or changes.
- `event` — one turn summary; its `id:` is the cursor to resume from.
- `status` — the investigation's status when the stream opens and whenever it changes.
- `end` — the run reached `completed` or `failed` and every event has been sent; the stream closes.
- `access_lost` — you may no longer see this investigation; the stream closes.

A stream closes after about five minutes so access is checked again; reconnect (SSE clients do this
themselves) and it resumes from the last event id. Comment lines are heartbeats.

WorkflowTemplate.title: WorkflowTemplate
WorkflowTemplate.description:
One curated workflow template.

Carries the full block graph rather than metadata alone: every consumer of the
list (preview modal, tier gating, search-to-workflow) reads ``blocks``, and the
catalog is small enough that splitting it into a second round-trip per card
would cost more than it saves.

WorkflowTemplateUpdate.title: WorkflowTemplateUpdate
WorkflowTemplateUpdate.description:
A partial edit. Every field optional; omitted fields are left alone.

The graph fields carry the same ``Block``/``WorkflowEdge`` models as the write
model: PATCH writes the same jsonb columns, so an edit must not be able to store a
shape a create would have refused.

blocks.title: Blocks
blocks.description: The template's block graph, in workflow-builder shape.

WorkflowTemplateWrite.title: WorkflowTemplateWrite
WorkflowTemplateWrite.description:
A template an org authors. No ownership fields: see the module docstring.

The graph is validated with the same ``Block``/``WorkflowEdge`` models that
``POST /workflows`` uses. A template is a workflow definition waiting to be
instantiated, so a shape this endpoint accepts but that endpoint rejects is a
template nobody can run -- and the failure would surface at render or run time,
a tenant's jsonb columns away from the request that caused it.

WorkspaceActionRequest.title: WorkspaceActionRequest
WorkspaceActionRequest.description:
Focus a tab, open an artifact, or close the viewer.

Focus-changing actions carry the counter the caller observed, so they land while
the viewer is still where they saw it and are refused once it has moved.
It counts focus changes only, so unrelated workspace writes -- registering
a workflow, renaming one -- do not reject a click that raced nothing. It
remains optional for legacy callers.
``open_workflow`` carries a workflow id rather than a handle, because an
inline card can be older than the roster it is asking to move.
``open_run`` carries both ids so the server can verify and focus the exact
execution represented by an inline run card. Workflow actions require the
session-pinned viewer capability; search actions do not.
